skill.name: Same plot, new setting
skill.why: Moving a story somewhere new makes an old plot feel fresh and funny.
skill.how: Keep the main events. Change the place and time, and every detail that goes with them.

steps.say: The Gingerbread Man: a biscuit man jumps out of the oven and runs. A fox tricks him.

show.text: In a cottage by the woods,
a gingerbread man jumps out of the oven
show.nudge: That's what happens. Which part tells you where?
That's what happens next. Which part tells you where?

steps.ask: Tap the part that tells you where it happens.
steps.win: Yes! Where and when is the setting. What happens is the plot.

steps.say: Now let's move it. Same plot, but a new place: a space station!
show: out of the oven and gets away.
steps.ask: What stayed the same as the old story?

options.reason: The cottage is gone. Where is he now?

options.text: He jumps out of the oven and gets away.

options.reason: Floating is new! It changed because of space. What didn't change?

steps.win: Yes! The plot stayed. Only the setting moved. Floating is a new detail that fits space.

steps.say: Every detail has to fit the new place. In the old story, a fox tricks him.

show.text: A fox tricks the gingerbread man.

steps.ask: What should trick him on the space station?

options.text: a fox hiding in the woods
options.reason: That is the old setting. There are no woods on a space station.

options.text: a pirate on a ship at sea
options.reason: That's a different new place. Stick to space.

options.text: a robot vacuum that sucks up everything

steps.win: Yes! The vacuum does the fox's job, and it belongs in space. New place, new details.

steps.say: Zed tried it too. He changed the place, but look at the rest of his line.

show.nudge: That's the new setting. Good! Which detail doesn't fit it?
He still runs. That's the plot. Which detail doesn't belong in space?

show.text: down the country lane past the cows.

steps.ask: Tap the detail that doesn't fit space.
steps.win: Yes! Cows in space? Changing the place name isn't enough. Every detail has to move too.

steps.say: Mo tried too. His story is in space. Now check what happens in it.

show.text: a gingerbread man opens a bakery and gets rich.

steps.ask: What went wrong in Mo's version?

options.reason: It's on a space station. That's new! Now check what happens.
Does anyone chase him? Does anything trick him? Check what happens.

steps.win: Right. Nobody chases him, so it's a new plot. Keep what happens. Change only where it happens.

steps.say: Your turn. Goldilocks: a girl sneaks into the bears' house and tries their things. The bears find her.
steps.ask: Which one keeps the plot but moves the setting?

options.text: Goldilocks eats the bears' porridge in their cottage, and they find her.
options.reason: Same plot, but it's still the cottage. Where's the new setting?

options.text: Goldilocks and three bears play games online and become best friends.
options.reason: That's a new plot. Nobody sneaks in, and nobody gets found.

options.text: Goldilocks sneaks into the bears' flat, tries their game controllers, and gets caught.

steps.win: Yes! Same sneaking in, same getting caught. New place, new details. Now move your own story.

terms.means: Where and when the story happens.
A detail from the old place. It doesn't fit the new one.
A detail that belongs in the new place.

examples.text: In a flat on Bear Street,

card.test: Check what happens: same as the old story? Check every detail: does it fit the new place?

weDo.frame: Tully is moving The Tortoise and the Hare to a footy oval.
weDo.prompt: Which detail fits the new setting?
weDo.hint: Which detail could only happen at a footy ground?
weDo.success: The pie and the canteen belong at the footy, and the hare still loses by stopping.

options.text: The hare stopped for a pie at the canteen, and the tortoise crossed the line.
The hare fell asleep under a tree beside the country road.
options.reason: That's the old setting. A country road isn't a footy oval.

options.text: The hare blasted off into the stars in her rocket.
options.reason: Rockets belong in space, not at the footy. Pick one new setting and stick to it.

weDo.frame: Tully wants a new version of a very old story.
weDo.text: The Boy Who Cried Wolf: a boy keeps faking wolf alarms. When a real wolf comes, nobody believes him.
weDo.prompt: Which retelling keeps the plot but moves it to a new setting?
weDo.hint: Check two things: what happens, and where it happens.
weDo.success: Faking alarms, then not being believed: same plot. The spaceship and aliens are the new setting.

options.text: A kid on a spaceship keeps faking alien alarms. When real aliens come, nobody believes him.
A kid on a spaceship finds an alien, and they become best friends.
options.reason: That's a whole new plot. Nobody lies, and nobody stops believing him.

options.text: A shepherd boy keeps crying wolf, and when a real wolf comes, nobody believes him.
options.reason: The plot is the same, but so is the setting. It's still sheep and wolves.

creature.name: Swapsum
creature.blurb: A possum that moves house every night, from gum tree to footy shed to spaceship. Wherever it lives, it gets up to exactly the same mischief.

workshop.mentor: Nobody was home at Number 3, Bear Street, but the front door was open and the TV was on. Goldie wandered in. On the couch sat three controllers. The first was sticky with tomato sauce. The second was so new it still had the plastic on. The third was just right. Goldie flopped into the smallest beanbag, loaded up the smallest bear's game and, in nine minutes flat, smashed his high score. Then the beanbag burst. Foam balls went everywhere. At that exact moment, the front door slammed. 'Someone's been using my controller,' growled Dad Bear. 'Someone's been sitting in my beanbag,' said Mum Bear. 'Someone,' wailed Baby Bear, staring at the screen, 'has beaten my high score, and she's still here!'
workshop.ask: Move a familiar plot somewhere new. Ideas: Goldilocks in Maxx's mansion, the Three Little Pigs at footy camp, Jack and the Beanstalk in space, Red Riding Hood underwater.
checklist: I kept the main events of the old story.
I moved it to a new place or time.
I changed the details to fit the new setting.
I stuck to one new setting all the way.
